uniequip_002_rmixer:
'Where did you get this feather duster?' Fiammetta asks in annoyance as she takes out the scarlet duster.
Patrizion lifts his head to answer as he wipes his armor: 'Oh, you mean Fifi? It was a gift from your friend Mostima, said I could look at it whenever I missed you.'
'And why exactly did you give it my childhood nickname...?'
Seeing the woman's eyebrows scrunched together in fury, Patrizion hesitates a moment, then decides to spit out the truth: 'Everyone thought it looked just like you, so I called it that.'
'Which part of this is meant to be like me?!' She raises the duster and gives it a few flicks, grumping disapprovingly.
'It's the same color as your ear tufts, and when the plumes are sticking up, they look like how your hair would stand up after I combed it for you when you were little.'
'Just throw it away!'
'Now that won't do. It was a gift, so throwing it away would be rude.' The old man takes the duster away from her, sticking it back into the old helmet before nodding in satisfaction. 'Yes, I'd say it looks quite nice in there, otherwise this armor would be rather lonely at home.'
'Then stick some flowers in there, or hang your medals on it or something!'
'But I'm such a humble man, how could I just put my medals on display like that?'
'Then what'll it take for you to put it away?!' The woman tries to snatch the feather duster back, but her every attempt is easily thwarted by the old man.
'No, no, I shan't no matter what you say. It's Fifi who keeps me company when you're not home. When it's movie time, she sits there quietly, never muttering about hackneyed plots or wooden acting or stale popcorn.'
After staring each other down for a good long while, she figures there is no reasoning with him. All she can do is pinch her brow.
'...Fine. There's no talking you out of this. Forget it.'
Upon hearing these words, the old man lets out the smile of a winner, but the smile soon stiffens as the woman changes tack.
'At first, I was going to take a whole month off to relax at home, maybe spend some time with you while I was at it.' She shakes her head and sighs as she continues: 'But since you have Fifi now, I guess I'll just have to go on a trip alone. Wouldn't want to disturb your leisure time, after all—'
Before she even finishes, the old man quickly grabs the feather duster, walks forward a few steps to pull open the storage room door, then throws it in before slamming the door shut.
'Ah, it's just a feather duster, no need to keep it on display.'
'But it was so pretty when stuck in the helmet.'
'What was pretty about it? It looks like it was caught in an explosion.'
'Wasn't it nice and quiet?'
'Movie time should be all about eating popcorn while grumbling with your fellow watchers.'
'Wasn't it just like me?'
*sigh* 'Don't mock an old man...' The old man tousles the woman's hair, smiling in exasperation. 'Fia, it's not that it's just like you, it was me thinking of you, that's all.'
uniequip_003_rmixer:
The schedule at the Shrine of Nurtury never changes. Eight in the evening: Patrizion has already taken off his armor, and he opens the door with his left hand, because his right is entirely taken up by two hand-exercise balls. Half past eight: Patrizion sinks into the sofa, opens his palm, and begins to examine those two peculiar hand-exercise balls in detail—or rather, one ball cactus and one spherical grenade. Ever since he found the two strange things in his home, Patrizion has been trying to work out where they came from.
Handing someone a grenade as a hand-exercise ball—it does sound like a prank he would pull, but who was he meaning to give it to? Certainly not Pag; that man sleeps with a gun in his arms of his own accord, and a prank like this would never get a rise out of him. Besides, how many years has it been since the two of them last spoke?
As for that ball cactus... it has very nearly become Patrizion's greatest preoccupation. Giovanni retired long ago, and the cactus tarts at every buffet reception are prepared for Patrizion alone. Velliv has teased him about it many times, and yet he cannot even say why he grew so partial to cactus in the first place.
He must have forgotten something.
And so, when the Patriarch expounds that order which embraces all things, when she speaks of that future without estrangement, without forgetting, without parting, Patrizion never weeps the way the faithful beside him do.
He knows that something must be missing from that future—the target of the grenade prank, the culprit who made him fond of cactus. He knows what Gia died for, and he knows why Pag left him. But this one person alone he can neither recall nor account for: he does not know who they were, nor how they vanished.
Every definite price he has been able to talk himself into accepting, and accept them he did. But a gap whose nature he does not know, whose origin he does not know—how is he to talk himself into accepting that?
And so, whenever the emotion of tens of thousands pours down the halo and into his brain, Patrizion grips those two hand-exercise balls tight, using the sting in his palm to remind himself that the future the Patriarch promises must still be missing something.

'Should I be moved, Patrizion?'
'Say that again and I'm blocking you, Your Holiness.'
'At least give me the grenade, won't you? It was meant for me all along, wasn't it—in return for the ball cactus I gave you back then.'
'You know what? I've suddenly decided I ought to pack the powder back in before I hand it over.'
'But truly, Patrizion. Knowing that you have kept your guard up against the Patriarch all this while because you sensed that I had vanished... I find it rather gratifying all the same.'
'All I realized was that someone had vanished; I never recalled that it was you. I cannot pay a price when I do not even know what it is, that is all. Had I remembered back then that the one who vanished was you, I might well have thrown myself wholeheartedly into helping the Patriarch.'
'Thank the Lord you did not remember.'
'Thank the Lord I did not remember.'
